author: kayleigh_drummond
subject: Another package gone off our porch
body: Another box disappeared off our front porch this morning, the second one since the start of the month. The delivery app said it was left at 11:40 and we did not get home until after four. Our camera caught a gray hatchback slowing at the end of the walk, but the plate is too blurry to read. Is anyone else on Hollinger Court or Pemberly Row seeing this? We are thinking about a parcel locker or having things sent to a store.

comments.author: marguerite_o
comments.body: Oh no, Kayleigh! We lost one in the spring. Our neighbors started leaving packages in the back hall by the side gate, and that has helped. Some of the delivery services also let you pick a drop spot in the app.

comments.author: curtis_bell
comments.body: Two things worked for us: pick the signature-required option or a pickup at the store, and don't leave the flattened boxes out for the whole week. A cheap doorbell camera aimed at the walk helps more than you'd think for plates.

comments.author: kayleigh_drummond
comments.body: Thanks Marguerite! Which side gate do you use? Ours has a tall fence and I'm not sure it would work.

comments.author: kwame_ofori
comments.body: Kayleigh, the porch pirate must be on a diet, he only takes the big boxes. Sorry this happened to you, for real.

comments.author: ruben_villamizar
comments.body: Most delivery services will send to a locker or a store. The closest pickup spot is listed in the app under the delivery options, and it takes about two minutes to change. I'd do that for the next few weeks.

author: benito_ruiz
subject: Gray sedan circling Ferrier Lane last night
body: A gray four-door sedan, an older model with a dented rear bumper, drove the loop on Ferrier Lane three times between 9 and 10 last night. It slowed at every driveway and never stopped. The back had no plate, only a paper temporary tag in the rear window. I was walking the dog and did not want to stare, so please check your doorbell camera clips from last night.

comments.author: dorothy_breen
comments.body: Sorry, I'm new here so I may be wrong, but I think I saw a car like that by the park on Saturday. I hope that helps a little.

comments.author: shirin_bahrami
comments.body: Benito, a car with a paper tag and no plate is worth calling in. Give the non-emergency line the color, the bumper damage, the time, and the direction it turned. Next time, write down the temp tag number if you can see it.

comments.author: ruben_villamizar
comments.body: A car like that was reported on Duncombe Lane in the spring. If you give the non-emergency line the time and the tag, they can pull that earlier report and connect the two.

comments.author: benito_ruiz
comments.body: Thanks Shirin. I'll call it in tomorrow morning. I should have grabbed the temp tag number when I had the chance.

comments.author: gunnar_sorensen
comments.body: Probably a contractor looking for the one job with nobody home. I'd still call it in, but I'm not losing sleep over it.

author: priya_lakhani
subject: Three cars broken into on Sawtell Court
body: Three cars parked on Sawtell Court were broken into last Thursday night, all on the street and none in a driveway. Ours had the glovebox emptied and the window shattered, and nothing was taken except loose change. The family three doors down lost a backpack with a laptop inside. Please lock your cars and take bags inside, even if you are only stopping for a minute. Thank you all.

comments.author: tomasz_wojcik
comments.body: Lock em. Had it happen in 2019. Nothing I could do after except file a report and replace the glass. Get the report number, you'll need it for insurance.

comments.author: odessa_wright
comments.body: Quick tip: most insurers want the police report number within a few days, so write it on a card in the glovebox. A dash cam clip also helps if you have one.

comments.author: henrik_dahl
comments.body: I had three of these on my block in one year, roughly nine hundred dollars in glass and repairs. Keep your receipts from the glass shop, because the insurance people will ask for them.

comments.author: priya_lakhani
comments.body: Thanks Odessa, I'll put the report number in the glovebox today.

comments.author: jolene_harkins
comments.body: My sister on Quaney Street said a silver sedan was seen trying car doors the same night. Not sure it's connected, but I thought you should know.

comments.author: wendell_pike
comments.body: Ask dispatch for the incident number, not only the report. The county dispatch log is public and shows what was called in on each block, so you can check whether a pattern is forming.

author: otis_whitfield
subject: lost beagle mix, answers to bo
body: lost. brown and white beagle mix named bo, about thirty pounds, slipped out the side gate on morrow court around six this evening. he has a red collar with a tag but he is not chipped yet. last seen heading toward the creek path behind the school. please check sheds and garages. if you see him call the number on my post, i will come with the truck.

comments.author: fiona_rawlings
comments.body: Otis, I'm so sorry. Walk the creek path with a bag of treats and call his name slowly, beagles follow their nose and stop when they hear a voice they know. Check the drainage culvert too.

comments.author: kofi_mensah
comments.body: I can drive the north loop tonight with a flashlight. Text if you want me to swing by your street.

comments.author: mateo_gallegos
comments.body: I'll take the lower road and check the culverts on the way home. The creek path is a good call.

comments.author: lupe_ochoa
comments.body: Otis, Bo was found! A neighbor on Tibbets Court heard barking from her garden shed and called the number on the post. Mulberry Fork Veterinary Clinic on Brindle Road also checked him over that night and was great with him.

comments.author: otis_whitfield
comments.body: ok thank you lupe. he is home eating and the latch is fixed. thank you all.

comments.author: colleen_brandt
comments.body: Yay!! So happy for you, Otis! Thanks Lupe, Fiona, and Kofi by name, you all made my week. Give that boy a treat from me.

author: deb_halvorsen
subject: Phone scam pretending to be the power company
body: A man called my husband yesterday saying he was with the power company and our account would be shut off at five unless we paid right away with gift cards. He sounded rushed, and he used the right street name, which is what scared me. We hung up and called the number on the bill, and the company confirmed it was a scam. If you get a call like this, hang up and call the number printed on your bill yourself.

comments.author: hanna_lindgren
comments.body: A reminder that the utility never takes gift cards. I keep a note by the phone with our real account number so I can check fast. Thank you for posting this, Deb.

comments.author: benito_ruiz
comments.body: A neighbor on Quaney got the same call. Twenty minutes later the caller phoned back to ask whether she had bought the cards yet. Hang up on any repeat call.

comments.author: hal_brenneman
comments.body: Caller ID is a liar, a phone can show any number it likes. Hang up and call the office number on the bill, like checking a level twice before you cut the board.

comments.author: deb_halvorsen
comments.body: Thank you, Benito. Their caller had the wrong last four digits on the account, which is how we knew right away.

comments.author: marisol_quintero
comments.body: I've gotten three of these calls on my cell this week. I just let them ring now.

comments.author: wendell_pike
comments.body: The state consumer protection site posts a monthly list of phone scams, with the scripts they use. Bookmark it, and check the dates before you pass along a warning.

author: raj_pandey
subject: Coyote on the Knoll loop trail this morning
body: Saw a coyote trotting along the Knoll loop trail this morning around 6:30, maybe forty yards ahead of me. It was calm, looked right at me, then walked into the cattails by the drainage culvert. Full grown, grizzled gray coat, bushy tail hanging low. I didn't approach it. Has anyone else had sightings out there? I want to know if it's a loner or part of a pack before I bring the dog back.

comments.author: curtis_bell
comments.body: Coyotes are normal here. Keep your dog on a short leash near the cattails, don't run, and make yourself big and loud if one gets close. Small dogs and cats are the real risk. One animal is not a sign of a pack.

comments.author: lloyd_sutter
comments.body: Saw two of them last winter by the retention pond. I blame the leaf blowers, they chase the animals out of the yards and onto the trails.

comments.author: greta_oseland
comments.body: Two people posted a sighting near the bridge at dusk on the gardeners group too, so it may be one animal moving around the trail. Be careful after dark.

comments.author: raj_pandey
comments.body: Thanks Curtis. I'll keep Pika on a short line at the culvert from now on.

comments.author: ruben_villamizar
comments.body: The park district wildlife map is posted in the gardeners group. It marks the den areas, so you know where not to walk the dog at dawn.

author: wade_tanaka
subject: Catalytic converter cut off my truck overnight
body: Someone cut the catalytic converter off my pickup in the driveway on Cobbin Street last night, sometime between one and four in the morning. It took maybe ten minutes, and the exhaust is hanging now. My dog barked at nothing for an hour. The police said they see these every week. Does anybody know a shop that can bolt on a locking shield quickly?

comments.author: ivan_kuzmenko
comments.body: Sorry, Wade. Ask for a bolt-on aftermarket shield, plus a stamped VIN etch on the converter so it's harder to sell. Photograph the VIN plate before you go in. Parts from a salvage yard run far cheaper than the dealer.

comments.author: gunnar_sorensen
comments.body: Same thing happened to a contractor's van on my street last spring. Lock the driveway gate at night if you have one. Not much more you can do.

comments.author: lloyd_sutter
comments.body: Put a bright motion light on the drive and point it at the truck. They work in the dark, so light is the cheapest deterrent I know.

comments.author: wade_tanaka
comments.body: Thanks Ivan. I'm going to ask about the shield this week.

comments.author: harlan_dietz
comments.body: Slow to answer, sorry. Good luck with the repair, Wade. I hope the shop gets it back on the road quickly.

author: wendell_pike
subject: Should Tallgrass Ridge have a formal neighborhood watch?
body: The public safety committee's agenda last month mentioned a volunteer observer pilot, but nothing was attached, and I have not found an ordinance for it. Before anyone signs up, we would need a sign-up sheet, a block captain per street, and written rules on what members can and cannot do. I'm happy to draft a one-page proposal if enough of you want one. For anyone who wants the background, the right-of-way ordinance is 24-088.

comments.author: bridget_mccourt
comments.body: Wendell, I'm thrilled and also a little worried. The last watch group on this side of town had a man with a clipboard taking pictures of kids on bikes. Write the rules first.

comments.author: tomasz_wojcik
comments.body: Pointless. We have the police. A clipboard does nothing except make people nervous. Pay for better lights and leave the rest alone.

comments.author: curtis_bell
comments.body: Respectfully, Tomasz, the fire department runs block captain programs in some towns because police can't be on every street at once. The main value is a phone tree and someone to check on an elderly neighbor.

comments.author: mateo_gallegos
comments.body: I'd sign up for a phone tree. I don't want anyone patrolling, I just want to know who to call if a car sits out front all night.

comments.author: rosalind_vance
comments.body: A written charter is essential. The phrase 'volunteer observer' carries legal exposure if it results in confrontation. I would support the one-page proposal, Wendell. Rosalind Vance.

comments.author: kwame_ofori
comments.body: Wendell, the only watch I trust is my wristwatch, and I'm late for it already.

comments.author: wendell_pike
comments.body: Tomasz, a watch would not replace patrols. I'd want the charter to say plainly that nobody follows anyone. The draft comes Friday.

author: ngozi_adeyemi
subject: Man trying car handles on Dunmore Terrace right now
body: Just called it in. A man in a dark hoodie is trying the door handles on the cars parked on Dunmore Terrace, and he is working down the block from the north end. He has a flashlight. Please stay inside and do not go out to confront him. I'm on the phone with the non-emergency line and they said a car is on the way. If you have a camera on that side, check it and send me the clip.

comments.author: paulina_ferraro
comments.body: Praying you're all safe. I'm two streets over and just locked everything. Thank you for posting.

comments.author: odessa_wright
comments.body: Saw the same hoodie man on the Halsey lot on Tuesday. I reported it then and nobody followed up, so please keep this call on record.

comments.author: curtis_bell
comments.body: Good call not going out. If the car leaves, note the color, the plate, and which way it turns. Officers will ask for those first.

comments.author: ngozi_adeyemi
comments.body: Dispatch says two cruisers are coming. The man is gone and the car is still in the driveway. Thanks Curtis.

comments.author: wendell_pike
comments.body: For next time, post the cross street and the time. Dunmore Terrace has no camera pointed at the street, and the crew will want the exact block.

comments.author: marisol_quintero
comments.body: Texting my block now. Everyone check your car doors tonight.

comments.author: kayleigh_drummond
comments.body: Thank you for posting this, Ngozi. We locked the van and turned the porch light on.

author: casey_ostrander
subject: Got a 'package fee' text, is this a thing here?
body: I'm new to town and wanted to ask. Last week I got a text saying a parcel could not be delivered and asking me to pay a small fee through a link to reschedule. I didn't click it, but the link looked real. I checked the delivery app and nothing was pending. Is this common in Tallgrass Ridge, and did anybody else get one?

comments.author: corinne_avila
comments.body: Very common. The links are fake and they want card numbers. Report the text to your carrier and delete it. If you clicked anything, call your bank using the number on the back of your card, not the one in the text.

comments.author: ivan_kuzmenko
comments.body: Check the tracking inside the app of the store you actually ordered from. Never pay a fee through a text link. Forward the text to your carrier's spam reporting number.

comments.author: casey_ostrander
comments.body: Thanks Corinne! I'll call my bank tomorrow to be safe.

comments.author: bridget_mccourt
comments.body: Got THREE of these in one week, all with the same bad spelling. Now I screen every text that says delivery. Welcome to town, by the way!

comments.author: augustin_perrault
comments.body: These texts are better written than most of my email. Hover over any link before you tap it, and the web address is almost always wrong.

comments.author: casey_ostrander
comments.body: Oh, I'll hover from now on. Good to know before I started tapping things.

author: augustin_perrault
subject: Detached garage forced on Cobbin Street
body: Someone forced the side door of our detached garage on Cobbin Street sometime Saturday night. They took the leaf blower, two bicycles, and a tool chest that proved too heavy to carry very far. They left the hedge trimmers on the lawn, which I find more insulting than the theft. The frame is split and I have added a bolt, but I would like to hear how the rest of you secure your garages.

comments.author: brendan_doyle
comments.body: Get a deadbolt rated for the frame, not just the door. The strike plate and the screws into the framing are the weak point. I can come by and reinforce it for the price of a sandwich.

comments.author: samir_qureshi
comments.body: Sorry, that's awful. Did you file a report? Write down the serial numbers for the bikes if you have them, they're the only way to trace them back.

comments.author: augustin_perrault
comments.body: Reported. I have the serial on one bike and not the other. The tool chest was too heavy to carry far, which is the only consolation.

comments.author: curtis_bell
comments.body: Put a motion light over the garage door and photograph your tools with serial numbers, then store the photos off the property. A light is the cheapest deterrent for most garages.

comments.author: esther_lund
comments.body: So sorry. I hope you find your things.

author: bernadette_hughes
subject: Man at the door claiming to check the water heater
body: A man in a navy windbreaker came to my door this afternoon, saying he was from the water department and needed to check my water heater. He had no badge, no marked van, and a clipboard with no logo. I told him I would call the office, and I shut the door. He then went down Lintel Way to the next two houses. Please call the water office number on your bill if anyone says they are from a utility.

comments.author: odessa_wright
comments.body: Good call. Real utility workers carry ID and leave a door hanger when they're working on a block. Call the number on your bill, not whatever card he hands you.

comments.author: noel_brandvold
comments.body: Sorry, I'm new so this may be a dumb question, but how do I tell a real door hanger from a fake one?

comments.author: bernadette_hughes
comments.body: A genuine notice carries the utility's name, a work order number, and a phone number you can verify yourself. A real worker will not mind if you call the office to confirm.

comments.author: benito_ruiz
comments.body: Mail carriers saw a navy windbreaker on Lintel Way last spring too. Nothing came of it, but keep a note of the time if you see him again.

comments.author: jonah_fitch
comments.body: I'll be the one asking for the clipboard next time. Real talk, glad you didn't let him in.
